note: Officeholders and districts as listed by the SF Department of Elections (sf.gov), the California State Senate, the SF Public Library's February 2026 legislator directory and Ballotpedia, checked Nov 4, 2026, the day after the Nov 3 general election. Results named here are preliminary election night counts and calls as reported by news outlets; the Department of Elections and Secretary of State results pages could not be opened in this session. Positions are the officials' own quoted words with the source and year. Nothing here is characterized or scored.
ballot_note: The Nov 3, 2026 general election was yesterday. Governor and the other statewide offices, the U.S. House seats for Districts 11 and 15, Assembly Districts 17 and 19 and Board of Equalization District 2 were on San Francisco ballots. The State Senate District 11 seat was not on the ballot. Results are preliminary and are counted for weeks; San Francisco expects to certify by Dec 3, 2026. Winners replace the names below once results are certified.
ward_reps_note: Assembly and U.S. House members for each supervisor district, from the registered voters each district has in those races (Department of Elections, Nov 3, 2026 district Statement of the Vote). Some districts are split between two.
review_note: Districts confirmed from sf.gov (page updated through Dec 2025) and the Nov 3, 2026 candidate list; boundaries under the Proposition 50 (2025) congressional map were not described by any official page opened. Results and calls are from news outlets, not the Department of Elections.

levels.title: Federal
levels.blurb: Two U.S. senators and two representatives. San Francisco is split between California's 11th and 15th Congressional Districts; which one is yours depends on your address (SF Department of Elections district lookup). Both districts were on the Nov 3, 2026 San Francisco ballot. The current congressional lines come from Proposition 50 (2025), per Ballotpedia.

levels.title: State
levels.blurb: The Governor (and the projected governor-elect), your State Senator (all of San Francisco is in Senate District 11, which also takes in part of San Mateo County), your Assembly member (the city is split between Assembly Districts 17 and 19) and your Board of Equalization member (District 2), which hears tax appeals and oversees some state taxes.

levels_note: San Francisco is a consolidated city and county, so there is no separate county government level; the Mayor, Board of Supervisors and citywide officers cover both roles and are in the city record.

becerra.name: Xavier Becerra
becerra.status: Projected winner of the Nov 3, 2026 governor's race. The SF Standard reports that the AP and NBC called the race for him at 8:03 p.m. Nov 3; NBC Bay Area's results page shows him as NBC News's projected winner. Statewide preliminary count as shown by the SF Standard on Nov 4, 7 a.m.: 4,992,161 votes (63.9%) to Steve Hilton's 2,815,459 (36.1%). Not yet in office.
becerra.caveat: No position statements gathered in this session. Results are preliminary until the Secretary of State certifies them.

wiener.name: Scott Wiener
wiener.status: District 11 covers all of San Francisco and part of San Mateo County. His Senate term runs to Dec 4, 2028 (Ballotpedia). He was on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot for U.S. House District 11 and led Connie Chan in preliminary results (87,641 to 70,511, about half the vote counted, per KQED at 11:53 p.m. Nov 3); not called as of the morning of Nov 4. If he wins, the Senate seat would become vacant.
